We generally sign vendor addenda if the clauses are materially aligned; if you prefer we can counter with our vendor addendum (attached) that includes:

- explicit limited-use / no-sale language
- data retention windows and deletion SLOs for request logs and telemetry
- subprocessor disclosure and 30-day notice for new subprocessors
- carve-outs for operational telemetry needed to maintain model serving (hashed/aggregated)

I'm attaching: Redwood_subprocessors_20260219.csv (current roster), SOC2_report_redwood_2025.pdf (most recent) and a draft redline to your addendum (redline_uspa_addendum_jonas_v1.docx).

Linda — Neha from Legal. I reviewed Jonas' redline and GreenMart draft. Narrow points:

- Service provider: we can accept the language as written but propose an explicit limited-use paragraph mirroring CA Civil Code § 1798.140(t)(2) language (we included suggested text in the attached redline).
- Subprocessors: we provide an up-to-date CSV and will provide onboarding evidence (vendor questionnaires and SOC2 excerpts) on a best-effort basis; for high-risk subprocessors we can provide standalone attestations.
- Notice period: 30 days' notice for material new subprocessors is our standard; if GreenMart requires pre-approval for a small list of named subprocessors we can accept a carve-in for that list.
- Deletion/Retention SLAs: request-level logs (PII associated with a request) — we will purge within 30 days after termination unless retention is contractually required; operational telemetry used for model performance is retained in aggregated, pseudonymized form and can be retained up to 12 months by default.

Could GreenMart confirm whether their addendum requires absolute deletion of all telemetry or allows aggregated telemetry retention for service quality and safety? That affects the redline.
